summary: Construct callable ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline basis functions.

capability: Construct a list of callable ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline basis functions.
operation: basis selector and constructor options -> list of callable basis functions
discovery.model: Caller-selected ascending-power polynomial or C2 cubic-spline basis; the polynomial default has three basis functions (powers 0, 1 and 2), while the spline default has five knots and four intervals.
discovery.geometry: One-dimensional scalar abscissa and ordinate samples; the returned evaluators are agnostic to the caller's coherent coordinate and ordinate units.
discovery.boundary: Spline evaluation is zero for finite queries outside the finite knot interval; nonfinite queries are zero-filled. Nonzero endpoint slopes are not a homogeneous basis and are rejected; unsupported factory selections are not approximated.

identity.direction: Declared inputs to List of independent basis evaluators
identity.definition: Construct a list of ascending-power polynomial or cubic-spline evaluators
identity.model: Basis-map selection with poly_deg=3 or n_knots=5 defaults
identity.geometry: one-dimensional scalar abscissa and ordinate samples
identity.boundary: Spline evaluation is zero outside the finite knot interval; no extrapolation is performed.
assumptions: Finite constructor samples and boundary-specific assumptions
Polynomial coefficients are ascending-power columns; poly_deg counts each function's coefficients, so poly_deg default3 means three functions of degree at most 2
Spline controls default to n_knots=5 and domain=(0,1); supplied xdata/ydata arrays must match
Clamped spline bases require yp=0; nonzero slopes define an affine family, not a linear basis
The second-clamped default basis omits the origin identity column and therefore has n_knots-1 columns
For spline selections, finite queries outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite query values use the zero-fill convention; polynomial selections evaluate directly

inputs.name: poly_deg
inputs.description: Ascending-power coefficients per basis function; the polynomial degree is poly_deg - 1
inputs.constraints: Polynomial selection only; an omitted value is 3, which yields three functions of degree at most 2

inputs.name: coeffs
inputs.description: Ascending-power coefficient columns, one per basis function; row j holds the coefficient of x**j
inputs.constraints: Polynomial selection only; an omitted value builds the poly_deg-row identity columns

inputs.name: n_knots
inputs.constraints: Spline selections only; an omitted value is 5; at least 3

inputs.name: domain
inputs.description: Closed knot interval used when xdata is omitted
inputs.constraints: Spline selections only; exactly two finite, increasing bounds; an omitted value is (0, 1)

inputs.name: xdata
inputs.constraints: Spline selections only; finite, strictly increasing N>=3; an omitted value builds n_knots equally spaced knots over domain

inputs.name: ydata
inputs.constraints: Spline selections only; finite, matching xdata; an omitted value builds the n_knots identity columns, without the first column for clamped_cubic_spline2

inputs.name: yp
inputs.description: Endpoint slopes, accepted only at zero
inputs.shape: (2,) for clamped_cubic_spline and scalar for clamped_cubic_spline1
inputs.constraints: clamped_cubic_spline and clamped_cubic_spline1 only; zero only, a nonzero slope is rejected; an omitted value uses the class default, also zero

inputs.name: m
inputs.description: Coefficient of the cylindrical Robin row
inputs.constraints: clamped_cubic_spline1 and clamped_cubic_spline2 only; finite; an omitted value uses the class default 0 and 1 respectively

outputs.name: basis_fns
outputs.constraints: Polynomial or spline callables; spline callables zero-fill finite values outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite queries

preconditions: Finite constructor samples and boundary-specific assumptions
Polynomial coefficients are ascending-power columns; poly_deg counts each function's coefficients, so poly_deg default3 means three functions of degree at most 2
Spline controls default to n_knots=5 and domain=(0,1); supplied xdata/ydata arrays must match
Clamped spline bases require yp=0; nonzero slopes define an affine family, not a linear basis
The second-clamped default basis omits the origin identity column and therefore has n_knots-1 columns
For spline selections, finite queries outside the closed knot interval and nonfinite query values use the zero-fill convention; polynomial selections evaluate directly
supported: Finite polynomial and spline basis selections implemented by scirel.numerics.basis
excluded: Quartic and special-function factory selections are rejected; no invented implementations
Physical special-spline closures and unsupported knot domains remain unresolved
Nonzero endpoint slopes for clamped basis construction are rejected
For spline selections, nonfinite query values are outside the numerical qualification and are zero-filled as a compatibility convention; polynomial selections evaluate directly

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises TypeError when a control is supplied that the selected basis does not implement, when an unknown keyword is supplied, and for a control of incompatible type; KeyError for an unregistered selector; NotImplementedError for an unsupported retained selector; and ValueError for a domain that is not exactly two finite bounds or for invalid spline samples/knots/boundary parameters. Linear-system failures propagate. Nonzero clamped endpoint slopes raise ValueError because they define an affine family. With assertions enabled, the retained clamped-spline constructor raises AssertionError when its endpoint-slope vector does not have length two.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Numerical linear-algebra or optional SciPy special-function exceptions propagate from evaluation.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; basis construction and evaluation are direct computations without an iterative convergence claim.
failure_semantics.partial_results: A failed constructor returns no evaluator; for spline selections, finite values outside the knot interval and nonfinite query values follow the zero-fill convention, while polynomial selections evaluate directly.

python.signature: build_basis(basis='poly', *, poly_deg=None, coeffs=None, n_knots=None, domain=None, xdata=None, ydata=None, yp=None, m=None)

example.description: Build the default ascending-power polynomial evaluators and evaluate all three at x=0.5.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.numerics.basis import build_basis

evaluators = build_basis()
assert len(evaluators) == 3
np.testing.assert_allclose([fn(0.5) for fn in evaluators], [1.0, 0.5, 0.25])
example.expected: Three evaluators are returned; their values at 0.5 are [1.0, 0.5, 0.25].

scope: Public callable signature and documented finite-input behavior
The direct regression fixtures listed in verification.tests
The executable example stored in this contract

Independent evidence (test_basis_design_evidence): the polynomial design matrix is compared with the closed-form Vandermonde matrix A[i, j] = x_i ** j; the cardinal spline bases are checked for partition of unity, which follows analytically from the constant satisfying each family's boundary rows; the second-clamped default basis is checked to carry n_knots - 1 columns and to be a linear subspace that merely omits the constant function; homogeneity and superposition are asserted directly for the second-clamped and the zero-slope clamped families, and refuted for the clamped family with a fixed nonzero endpoint slope, which the builder rejects; and the declared zero-fill convention is probed one representable step outside the knot interval.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Direct examples and named regression fixtures establish the documented relation on those inputs; they do not establish arbitrary-input correctness or experimental validation. C1 evidence adds: Factory members checked against closed-form powers and against the cardinal partition-of-unity identity.
known_limitations: Quartic and special-function factory selections are rejected; no invented implementations
Physical special-spline closures and unsupported knot domains remain unresolved
Nonzero clamped endpoint slopes are outside the linear-basis contract
For spline selections, nonfinite query values are outside the numerical qualification and are zero-filled as a compatibility convention; polynomial selections evaluate directly

Three failure channels of the basis factory differ from the api-spec convention (an unregistered selector raises KeyError, a list coeffs control raises AttributeError, and a 1-D coeffs array raises IndexError); this contract records only what is observed and promises none of those types. The correction is a behaviour change tracked in tickets/convention/T-2026-0002.md, which also covers whether an unsupported retained selector should raise NotImplementedError.

The second-clamped default basis is a linear subspace, not an affine family: fixing y_data[0] = 0 removes one degree of freedom and the slope system is homogeneous in the ordinates, so spline(2 y) = 2 spline(y) and spline(y1 + y2) = spline(y1) + spline(y2) both hold. It omits the constant function, which is why its columns do not sum to one, but that absence is not evidence of an affine offset. The plain clamped family is linear only at yp = (0, 0), which the basis builder enforces, and affine with a fixed nonzero yp, which the builder rejects; a nonzero slope contributes a constant term rather than scaling with the ordinates.

basis.statement: Factory members are checked against closed-form powers and against the cardinal partition-of-unity identity.
